details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1190 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `sed`-based log-tail extraction is brittle because it depends on an exact hardcoded marker string and will silently fall back to full-log classification if that match stops working.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers flagged the same root cause; if the marker text changes or the extraction fails, stale pre-rerender log entries can again influence `classify_preflight_failure`, though reviewers disagreed on severity and impact.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:1189-1195 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The temporary log slice is written without explicit handling for `sed`/redirection failure or unwritable runtime paths.
  WHY: Reviewers agreed the current fail-open behavior can mask extraction problems; one reviewer said the script may abort under `set -e`, while others said it silently falls back, so the highest severity and the disagreement are noted.
- tests/test_validate_process_render_recovery.py:89-782 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The test file contains multiple embedded copies of the production shell logic, creating significant drift and maintenance risk.
  WHY: All reviewers identified the same duplication pattern across the heredoc test blocks; if production logic changes and one copy is missed, tests can validate stale behavior.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh lines 1186-1195 | severity=critical | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `sed` pattern uses `[.]` to escape the period, which is unconventional and brittle.
  WHY: If the marker line changes or appears multiple times, the extraction can fail silently and fall back to scanning the full log, which can misclassify pre-flight failures.
- tests/test_validate_process_render_recovery.py | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test file contains multiple copies of the production logic embedded in heredocs across different test functions.
  WHY: This creates a maintenance burden where any change to the production logic must be manually updated in multiple test locations.
- scripts/validate_process.sh lines 1178-1185 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The logic creates a temporary log file but doesn't clean it up.
  WHY: Although it is in `RUNTIME_DIR`, it may accumulate if that directory is not cleaned elsewhere.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh Line or code reference: 1190 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The tail-slicing logic using `sed -n '/pattern/,$p'` is brittle and can lead to incorrect failure classification if multiple recovery attempts occur or if the marker string is slightly modified.
  WHY: If the marker appears more than once, `sed` matches from the first occurrence; if the exact marker changes, `tmp_log` becomes empty and the script silently falls back to full-log scanning.
- tests/test_validate_process_render_recovery.py Line or code reference: Multiple locations (lines 136, 293, 430, 584, 740 etc.) | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Extreme code duplication of production shell logic within Python test heredocs.
  WHY: The test file copies the shell function into multiple `MOCK_VALIDATE_PROCESS` blocks, so a future production fix can be missed in one copy and leave tests validating stale behavior.
- scripts/validate_process.sh Line or code reference: 1189-1191 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The script writes to `${RUNTIME_DIR}/preflight_latest.log` without verifying that the directory is writable.
  WHY: If the write fails, the code falls back to `classify_preflight_failure` on the original full log and hides the fact that the intended log slicing failed.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `sed` extraction logic works correctly but has minor brittleness.
  WHY: The `[.]` character class is unconventional, there is no explicit error checking for `sed` failure, and the hardcoded marker string will stop matching if the echoed message changes.
- tests/test_test_validate_process_render_duplicate_recovery. py | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test file embeds 6 identical copies of the 6-line sed extraction block.
  WHY: Any future change to the production logic must be mirrored across all test copies, creating maintenance burden and drift risk.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- tests/test_validate_process_render_recovery.py | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test file embeds 6 copies of the `attempt_render_recovery_after_preflight_failure` shell function in heredocs.
  WHY: Every production change to that function must be mirrored across all 6 test cases, creating significant maintenance burden and drift risk.
- scripts/validate_process.sh | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `sed -n '/Render recovery: rerender completed; re-running pre-flight checks[.]/,$p'` hardcodes the marker pattern.
  WHY: `[.]` is valid but unconventional, and if the echoed marker changes the `sed` pattern will silently fail and fall back to scanning the full log.
- scripts/validate_process.sh | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The temp file write and `sed` invocation have no validation of exit status or temp-file creation.
  WHY: If `sed` fails or `RUNTIME_DIR` is unwritable, the code cannot distinguish extraction failure from an empty result and falls back to full-log classification.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `sed` extraction writes to `${tmp_log}` without any guard.
  WHY: Under `set -e`, a redirection or `sed` failure can exit the script immediately and bypass the intended fail-open fallback to full-log classification.
- scripts/validate_process.sh | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `sed` pattern uses `[.]` to match a literal trailing period.
  WHY: This is behaviorally correct but unconventional; a fixed-string match or `\.` would be clearer and slightly more efficient.
- tests/test_validate_process_render_recovery.py | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test duplicates the production `attempt_render_recovery_after_preflight_failure` function across five embedded shell blocks.
  WHY: Manual duplication creates ongoing maintenance drift risk even though all copies were updated this cycle.
=== END FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
